statement: For the 0/1 knapsack problem, sorting the items by decreasing value-to-weight ratio and greedily taking every item that still fits yields an optimal solution.
definitions: Instance = capacity W and items with positive integer weight and value; a feasible solution is a subset of total weight <= W; optimal = maximum total value. Greedy = scan items in non-increasing value/weight ratio (ties arbitrary) and take an item iff it fits in the remaining capacity.
ground_truth_witness: Capacity W = 10 with two items: A = (weight 1, value 2, ratio 2) and B = (weight 10, value 15, ratio 1.5). Ratio-greedy takes A first (total weight 1, value 2); B no longer fits (1 + 10 > 10), so greedy stops with value 2. Taking only B is feasible (weight 10 <= 10) and has value 15, so greedy is off by a factor of 7.5 here and the ratio rule can be arbitrarily bad without the 'best single item' correction.
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records
